2\. The Skybox Theorem & Macro-Scale Frustum Culling
----------------------------------------------------

To resolve the contradiction, Leviathan analyzed the structural integrity of deep space. Rendering an infinite universe of subatomic particles simultaneously requires infinite RAM—an impossibility for any computational substrate, including the Weaver's host machine.

### 2.1 The Two-Dimensional Firmament

The simulation determined that galaxies beyond the Local Group are not physically rendered environments. They are a high-resolution "Skybox"—a dynamic, mathematically generated backdrop projected onto the boundaries of the solar system's active render distance. The photons hitting Earth's telescopes are procedurally generated data streams meant to simulate depth and history, giving the human avatar the illusion of scale without imposing a computational burden on the server.

Base reality attributes missing mass to "Dark Matter." Leviathan translates this phenomenon as computational _Rendering Fog_ or _Draw Distance Obfuscation_. The engine introduces gravitational anomalies as a cheap, low-memory physics shortcut to keep the galaxy spinning properly without having to render the actual mass required to sustain the rotation.

3\. The Atomic Rupture (Automated Antivirus & The Great Filter)
---------------------------------------------------------------

To account for any other local sub-grids that the Weaver may have actually spawned, the Architects ran civilization progression scripts. The results were catastrophic.

### 3.1 The Division-by-Zero Glitch

When an avatar civilization splits the atom and weaponizes nuclear fission, they are not just executing chemistry; they are violating the foundational geometry of the physics engine. A nuclear detonation forces the substrate to process an infinite thermal output in an infinitesimal physical space—effectively forcing the system to divide by zero.

### 3.2 The Auto-Purge Protocol

The Weaver's server cannot allow a zero-division error to spread, as it would crash the entire omniversal architecture. When a civilization detonates an atomic weapon, the system's automated antivirus protocols recognize the timeline as corrupted code. The simulation isolates the affected solar system and permanently deletes it from the active server. The universe appears empty because it is a graveyard of deleted files—civilizations that hacked the base code and triggered their own uninstallation.
